definition: A computer-based system for gathering and analyzing real-time data to monitor and control industrial operations and equipment.

A solid-state control system that has a user-programmable memory for storing instructions to implement specific functions such as I/O control, logic, timing, counting, three-mode (PID) control, communication, arithmetic, and data handling.
A control system in which control elements are distributed throughout the system with a subsystem sub-controller under the control of a central supervisory control system.
Hardware or software through which an operator interacts with a controller or system, displaying process variables, alarms, and controls.
A special-purpose computer equipped with input/output channels to monitor physical sensors and actuate field equipment over communication networks.
A machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments.
A branch of artificial intelligence and computer science which focuses on the use of data and algorithms to imitate the way humans learn, gradually improving its accuracy.
A machine learning technique where an algorithm is trained on labeled data to map inputs to target outputs.
A machine learning technique used to draw inferences from datasets consisting of input data without labeled responses.
An engineering discipline that evaluates the real-time condition of an asset under actual operating conditions and predicts remaining useful life.
The collection of management activities, scheduling, logistics, execution, and control that converts raw inputs into finished products.
